`/^https:/.test(url)` asks whether a string starts with a fixed text. `url.startsWith("https:")` asks the same in plain words, and the text needs no regex escaping.

The rule reports `.test()` on a regex literal that is only `^` followed by plain characters, or plain characters followed by `$`. A regex with the `m` flag, or with the `i` flag and letters, is not reported.

`--fix` rewrites the call when the argument is a name, a string, a property access or a call.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```js
const secure = /^https:/.test(url);
const isScript = /\.js$/.test(file);
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
const secure = url.startsWith("https:");
const isScript = file.endsWith(".js");

const isImage = /\.(png|jpg)$/.test(file);
const isHeader = /^x-/i.test(name);
```
